messages:
frank_oncall: heads-up — getting a support escalation: multiple customers reporting p99 API latency up ~3x from eu-west since ~12:30 UTC. Ticket IDs 8732 / 8733.

dave_support: customer says requests that normally tail ~120ms are hitting 700-1200ms and occasional timeouts. No obvious error spikes, just tail. They included trace ids.

carol_net: looking at edge metrics now — we see p95/p99 spike on eu-west POPs starting 12:28 UTC, TLS handshake time distribution shifted. CPU on ingress proxies is normal, but SYN->TLS time shows extra 300-600ms in some sessions.

alice.m: quick repro steps from support: `curl -w "%{time_connect} %{time_appconnect} %{time_total}\n" -sS -o /dev/null https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` returns `0.035 0.530 0.540` for some runs.

carol_net: ran a few traceroutes from a client probe in eu-west: `traceroute -n api.eu-west.redwood.ai` — there's an extra hop through AS65499 (transit partner) for a subset of flows, causing cross-az hairpin.

bob_sre: I see the same in our internal e2e probes: path A (good) is 5 hops -> POP -> origin; path B (bad) goes via IX -> remote POP -> back -> origin. That adds ~400ms for handshake.

erin_prod: any recent GSLB or weight changes? We rolled a subtle weight change for eu-west balancing at 12:15 to shift capacity during yesterday's surge.

carol_net: checking DNS/GSLB logs... yes, we pushed a weight update at 12:16 UTC that introduced a secondary steering policy for some prefixes; rollout was gradual and a subset of LBs started preferring the remote POP path. Could explain multi-POP hop.

frank_oncall: action: for immediate mitigation, revert the weight change or force local-pref routing for affected geo-tagged prefixes. Which is quickest?

bob_sre: revert is safest. I can rollback the GSLB weights to previous commit. If DNS TTL is low we might see churn, so also set a temporary static steering rule for customer IPs.

alice.m: support asked for a short-term client-side mitigation: increase SDK retry/backoff to mask single-handshake spikes. We should avoid recommending that as permanent fix though.

carol_net: started rollback of GSLB weights (initiated 12:56 UTC). Monitoring now. Also opened ticket with transit partner AS65499; their flow logs show sudden BGP path change at the same timeframe.

deploy-bot: revert-gslb-weights (sha: a1b2c3d) deployed by bob_sre at 12:57 UTC — rollout 0/3 -> 3/3.

bob_sre: rollback completed, propagation looks good in our authoritative metrics. Internal probes show p99 in eu-west dropping back toward baseline ~13:04 UTC.

dave_support: replied to customers with interim note and asked them to confirm. Two customers reported improvement ~13:06 UTC.

carol_net: follow-ups: 1) open CAP with transit partner to understand BGP flap that caused route detour; 2) add a GSLB pre-check to detect weight changes that could cause multi-POP hairpin (safety guard); 3) increase DNS steering TTL for critical API prefixes during peak deploy windows.

erin_prod: +1 on pre-check. Also we should add an automated probe that measures TLS handshake latency per-pop and alerts when handshake tail > 250ms for 5m.

bob_sre: I've created a follow-up ticket: SRE-INC-4721 with proposed mitigations and owners. I'll own rollback docs and the pre-check. carol_net will lead transit CAP. alice.m will coordinate postmortem notes for support comms.

frank_oncall: good triage. For the postmortem include: reproducible probe commands (curl/traceroute), sample trace ids, GSLB diff (before/after), and transit partner logs. Marking this as resolved for now — will keep thread open until CAP completes. :thumbsup:

dave_support: customers updated and closing support tickets after confirmation. Thanks team.

carol_net: CAP with AS65499 scheduled for 15:00 UTC. Adding action items to incident doc.

bob_sre: last note — consider adding a routing policy that prefers same-az POPs as a safety net when latency-sensitive routes are identified. Might require a short design doc.

frank_oncall: agreed. Tagging for design backlog. Closing out on-call handoff.
